title: A money value type
description:
Write a `readonly record struct Money(long Cents, string Currency)`. Storing whole cents avoids rounding problems.

```csharp
var price = Money.Parse("12.34 EUR");      // Cents = 1234, Currency = "EUR"
var total = price.Add(Money.Parse("0.66 EUR"));
total.ToString();                          // "13.00 EUR"
total.Allocate(3);                         // [4.34 EUR, 4.33 EUR, 4.33 EUR]: the parts add up exactly
total == new Money(1300, "EUR");           // true: value equality
total with { Currency = "USD" };           // a copy in another currency
```

- `Parse` reads `<amount> <currency>`: the amount has up to 2 decimals and may be negative (`"-5 EUR"`, `"3.5 USD"`), the currency is 3 capital letters. Anything else throws a `FormatException`.
- `Add` and `Subtract` throw an `InvalidOperationException` when the currencies differ.
- `ToString` writes the amount with 2 decimals and a `.`: `-0.05 EUR`.
- `Allocate(n)` splits into `n` parts that differ by at most one cent, larger parts first, and sum to the original. `n` must be 1 or more (else `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`). Assume the amount is not negative.
hints: Split the text at the space into the amount and the currency, then split the amount at `.`. Check that each piece is only digits, with one or two after the point, and that the currency is three letters from `A` to `Z`.
For `Allocate`, every part gets `Cents / parts`, and the first `Cents % parts` parts get one cent more.
